minimal_reproducer.reduction: five GftSmul instances and 798 LUT become three instances and 430-452 LUT -- 46 % smaller
minimal_reproducer.structure: u_ctrl = smul(live,TWO) and u_comm_a = smul(live,TWO) are the CONTROL (identical operand order); u_comm_b = smul(TWO,live) is the TEST. The two clauses differ in one respect: which port the constant folds into.
minimal_reproducer.the_failing_clause: c_self TRUE, c_comm FALSE -- exactly the pattern the 798-LUT design shows. Two instances with the SAME operand order always agree; the one with them swapped does not.

verdict_tracks_the_netlist_not_the_seed.observation: the two 430 LUT / 112 CARRY4 builds both PASS; the two 452 LUT / 105 CARRY4 builds both FAIL
verdict_tracks_the_netlist_not_the_seed.what_makes_the_two_netlists: t27c's fixed-point loop forces JTAG_CHAIN to whatever site nextpnr chose. Seeds 7 and 42 needed forcing to 2; seeds 1234 and 1 did not. The BSCANE2 chain index cannot reach the arithmetic, yet yosys maps 22 LUTs and 7 CARRY4 differently under it.
verdict_tracks_the_netlist_not_the_seed.significance: the seed sweep of W842/W977 was reading a netlist difference, not only a placement one -- another confound, found the same way as W981's

minimal_reproducer.seed_mapping_inverts: in the 798-LUT design seeds 1 and 42 PASS and 7 and 1234 FAIL; here 7 and 42 PASS and 1 and 1234 FAIL. The seed is not a property of the failure.

sat_proof_on_the_mapped_netlist.question: do the two swapped-operand cones compute the same function AFTER yosys has folded the constant and mapped to Xilinx primitives?
sat_proof_on_the_mapped_netlist.method: tri miter -- the miter is synthesised by the SAME script t27c runs (including the W813 `share` removal), then techmap -map +/xilinx/cells_sim.v gives the solver models for LUTn/CARRY4/MUXF7, then sat -verify -prove neq 1'b0
sat_proof_on_the_mapped_netlist.consequence: the netlist handed to nextpnr IS commutative. Synthesis is exonerated and the fault is at or below place-and-route. W977 proved commutativity on the MODULE; this proves it on the two FOLDED CONES that actually fail.

third_method_that_failed_its_control.method: recover each post-place-and-route LUT's logical function from nextpnr's --write JSON, undoing pin permutation with the X_ORIG_PORT_A* attributes, and compare name-matched cells
third_method_that_failed_its_control.control: seed 42 against seed 1 -- TWO BUILDS THAT BOTH PASS
third_method_that_failed_its_control.verdict: INCONCLUSIVE -- the control pair disagrees as much as the test pairs. Place-and-route repacks LUTs into slice halves and renames most cells, so name identity does not imply function identity.
third_method_that_failed_its_control.pattern: third cell-level method, third control-saved retraction: FASM INIT multisets (W981), post-PnR recovered functions (W982). Cell-level comparison cannot decide function preservation across a repacking placer.
third_method_that_failed_its_control.what_would_work: a whole-design equivalence over primary inputs and outputs, which needs semantic models for SLICE_LUTX, SLICE_FFX and CARRY4 as nextpnr emits them
